title: Information Technology Act, 2000 — Section 10A (Validity of Contracts Formed Through Electronic Means)

content.overview: Section 10A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 provides that where in a contract formation the communication of proposals, acceptance of proposals, revocation of proposals and acceptances, as the case may be, are expressed in electronic form or by means of an electronic record, such contract shall not be deemed to be unenforceable solely on the ground that such electronic form or means was used.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Was proposal/acceptance/revocation in electronic form? (2) Is the only objection the electronic medium? (3) Are general Contract Act formation rules still satisfied?
content.study:
s. 10A removes the electronic-medium objection. It does not dispense with offer, acceptance, consideration or other formation requirements under the Indian Contract Act.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: No unenforceability for electronic form alone
sections.body: A contract is not unenforceable solely because proposal, acceptance or revocation was expressed in electronic form or by electronic record.

sections.heading: Formation still required
sections.body: Offer, acceptance, intention, consideration and capacity under the Contract Act remain necessary; s. 10A only neutralises the medium objection.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: Covers communication of proposals, acceptances and revocations in electronic form.

sections.heading: Link to ss. 4–5
sections.body: Legal recognition of electronic records and signatures supports electronic contracting recognised under s. 10A.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Test Contract Act formation; then apply s. 10A to defeat a pure electronic-medium challenge.

provisions.title: Validity of contracts formed through electronic means

examples.title: Click-wrap acceptance
examples.body: Online acceptance of terms by electronic communication — if Contract Act formation is otherwise complete, s. 10A prevents unenforceability solely for electronic form.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 10A create a contract without acceptance?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. s. 10A only removes the electronic-form objection; acceptance and other formation elements remain essential.

distinctions.title: s. 10A vs Contract Act formation
distinctions.right: Supplies offer, acceptance, consideration and related formation rules.

misconceptions.trap: Electronic contracts are automatically valid under s. 10A alone.
misconceptions.correction: s. 10A only prevents unenforceability solely for electronic form; Contract Act formation must still be proved.
